method: Read first560 lines of pinned launcher; static dispatch, subprocess and resource-ownership review only. No command executed.
findings: launch returns unit; spawn failures and most ShellExecute/Windows action results are discarded. Caller cannot receive a structured success/failure result from this interface. Some file opening retries openas then notepad but final status still not returned.

Generic command execution splits whitespace, without quoted-argument parsing; control.exe arguments similarly split. Existing exact full paths take earlier shell-open branch, so this observation does not imply all paths with spaces fail. Quoted executable-plus-arguments behavior remains unqualified at runtime.

Focus session workers share global AtomicBool without generation or worker handle. Repeated starts can spawn multiple workers; restarting while an old worker sleeps can let old worker continue under new true flag. No worker lifetime control or runtime reproduction in this batch.

Sequential clipboard paste manually transfers global allocation to clipboard. Failure branches after allocation have no GlobalFree in reviewed body; it sends paste/Enter even when allocation/open/set failed. Correct ownership on successful SetClipboardData must not be treated as a leak. No clipboard/process/keyboard actions run.

ChatGPT URL launch spawns title-based window activation and repeated Enter injection; target is selected by title/process filter rather than browser-tab identity. No browsing or keyboard simulation performed.

kill PID dispatch does not revalidate process identity; protected-name filtering exists in search producer, not this dispatcher. PID reuse between presentation and invocation remains an untested lifecycle limitation. No process termination invoked.

Quit-other/hide-other actions capture current foreground window at execution time; whether launcher has restored previous foreground before this call requires unread main/caller review. No foreground-selection bug asserted as reproduced.

Recycle action uses no-confirmation flag in dispatcher. Whether caller provides a separate confirmation is outside this read batch. This source observation is not an instruction to execute or bypass confirmation.
This module contains system-action implementation rather than duplicate-content comparison. No local production change follows from its static review alone.
limits: No tests or Windows runtime executed in this batch; upstream/local test totals unchanged.
